system.effect:
A Zenith Move (shortened to Z-Move) is a special type of Move, in which a Trainer and their Pokémon's wishes combine to unleash an attack comprising the full power of both. The Trainer focuses their will into a stone known as a Zenith Core, which magnifies and transmits that innate power between a pair of Z-Crystals that both the Trainer and Pokémon hold, allowing the Pokemon to transform one of its Moves into a powerful Z-Move.

When a Pokémon attempts to use a Damaging Move with a Type corresponding to a Z-Crystal held by the Pokémon and the Trainer, the Trainer can transform that Move into a Z-Move as a Full Action Reaction. These Z-Moves are very powerful, but a Zenith Core can only fuel a single Z-Move per Scene. If an Interrupt is used so that the target is instead not hit by the move, the target instead takes damage as if 2 steps more resistant to the attack (just as Smite causes 1 more step of resistance for misses, these don’t stack, so using Protect against a miss is still only 2 steps more resistant on top of type matchups)

Note: If a Trainer is incapacitated before the Z-Move activation completely resolves, the Zenith Core’s charge is not expended and the Z-Move isn’t used, but the Trainer still uses their Full Action.

There are 18 different Z-Crystals that correspond to each of the 18 types, with several others that correspond to specific Pokémon. When a Trainer obtains a Z-Crystal that they can hold, they may then craft Z-Crystals that their Pokemon may hold. By default, a Trainer may only have the Zenith Core and one variety of Z-Crystal equipped at one time.

It is recommended for GMs to give a few Z-Crystals out to their players as valuable rewards for quests, prizes for winning tournaments, that sort of thing!
A Z-Ring or Z-Power Ring is also required in order to perform Z-Moves. A Pokémon can only use a Z-Move if its Trainer is wearing a Z-Ring or Z-Power Ring and has the same Z-Crystal the Pokémon is holding. Mega Evolved and Primal Pokémon cannot use Z-Moves, even when holding an appropriate Z-Crystal (such as after Transform).
